newsitem.title: MEXICO: Children also get the vote in Mexican elections.
newsitem.headline: Children also get the vote in Mexican elections.

text.p: They may not vote for political parties like adults, but Mexican children will fill out a ballot for the first time in Sunday's elections.
About eight million six to 12-year-olds are expected to go to the polls to pick one of a list of human rights they deem most important.

"The children are going to participate because they want to try out their vote to make their opinions known," said 10-year-old Sandra Jimenez, a wheelchair-bound participant of the United Nations Children's Fund (Unicef) programme in Mexico.
The rights the children will choose from include health, freedom of speech and living in peace with caring people.

Some 52 million Mexicans are registered to vote on Sunday to choose 500 federal deputies, 32 of 128 senators, governors in six states, and for the first time in modern history, the mayor of Mexico City.
Unicef and the independent Federal Electoral Institute (IFE), the country's main electoral body, decided to take advantage of the voting to organise a nationwide election for children.
"From the surveys we've done, the children are very interested," Unicef project coordinator Rafael Enriquez said.

The adult elections should also prove to be interesting. According to opinion polls, they are expected to deal the worst ever defeat to the Institutional Revolutionary Party, that has ruled Mexico for 68 years.

The youngsters can vote in 9,000 polls installed in parks, schools, health centres, sports sites, museums and malls across the country. Children between 13 and 18 years old will monitor the elections.
